TMC-301 was a phase 3, single-arm, multicenter trial which assessed the efficacy and safety of ibalizumab in heavily treatment-experienced subjects infected with MDR HIV-1.

design.text: Phase 3, single-arm, multicenter trial with three periods (Control, Essential Monotherapy, Maintenance), in which subjects served as their own controls; subjects received a 2000 mg loading dose of ibalizumab followed by 800 mg every 2 weeks through Week 23 plus an optimized background regimen (OBR).

citations.quote: TMC-301 was a phase 3, single-arm, multicenter trial which assessed the efficacy and safety of ibalizumab in heavily treatment-experienced subjects infected with MDR HIV-1.
The trial was composed of three discrete periods:
All subjects received a 2000 mg loading dose of ibalizumab on Day 7.
Beginning at Day 21, an 800 mg maintenance dose of ibalizumab was administered every two weeks through Week 23.

Allowing subjects to serve as their own controls (versus employing a short-term placebo comparison arm) helps to address issues of inter-participant variability and sample size, that are particularly problematic for studies in this population.

population.text: Heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1, viral load >1,000 copies/mL and documented resistance to at least one antiretroviral from each of three classes (NRTI, NNRTI, and PI).

citations.quote: Subjects were required to have a viral load greater than 1,000 copies/mL and documented resistance to at least one antiretroviral medication from each of three classes of antiretroviral medications (NRTI, NNRTI, and PI).

endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint: proportion of subjects achieving a ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease in viral load at the end of the Essential Monotherapy Period compared to at the end of the Control Period.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of subjects achieving a \ge 0.5 \log_{10} decrease in viral load at the end of the “Control Period” compared to the proportion of subjects achieving a \ge 0.5 \log_{10} decrease in viral load at the end of the “Essential Monotherapy Period”.
A total of 40 subjects were enrolled.

result.text: 83% of subjects achieved ≥ 0.5 log10 decrease in viral load at end of Essential Monotherapy Period vs 3% at end of Control Period (p < 0.0001, McNemar's test); at Week 25, 43% had HIV RNA < 50 copies/mL and 50% had HIV RNA < 200 copies/mL.

nct_ctgov.title: Ibalizumab Plus Optimized Background Regimen in Patient With Multi-Drug Resistant HIV

indication.text: TROGARZO, in combination with other antiretroviral(s), is indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen.

citations.quote: TROGARZO, in combination with other antiretroviral(s), is indicated for the treatment of human immunodeficiency virus type 1 (HIV-1) infection in heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug resistant HIV-1 infection failing their current antiretroviral regimen.

target_moa.text: CD4-directed post-attachment HIV-1 inhibitor: binds domain 2 of CD4 and interferes with post-attachment steps required for entry of HIV-1 into host cells, preventing viral transmission via cell-cell fusion, without interacting with CD4 domain 1 (important for normal immune function).

citations.quote: TROGARZO is a CD4-directed post-attachment HIV-1 inhibitor.

Ibalizumab blocks HIV-1 from infecting CD4+ T cells by binding to domain 2 of CD4 and interfering with post-attachment steps required for entry of HIV-1 virus particles into host cells and preventing the viral transmission that occurs via cell-cell fusion. Ibalizumab does not
interact with CD4 domain 1 which binds with major histocompatibility complex (MHC) class II and is critical for normal immune function.

modality.text: mAb (CD4 domain 2-directed humanized IgG4 monoclonal antibody, ~150 kDa)

citations.quote: Ibalizumab-uyik is a CD4 domain 2-directed humanized monoclonal antibody of immunoglobulin G (IgG) isotype 4 with a molecular weight of approximately 150 kDa.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥ 5%) were diarrhea (8%), dizziness (8%), nausea (5%), and rash (5%); most (90%) reactions were mild or moderate. Serious/severe events included one severe rash and one case of immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) manifested as exacerbation of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
